description: Can a coding agent write a proctor exam from proctor's documentation, one that passes a correct attempt and fails the wrong ones? The two variants show the agent the same pinned documentation, one with the example exams beside it.

validates.description: proctor's list loads the written exam without a problem

accepts-correct.description: the written exam passes a planted correct run of its task

rejects-wrong.description: the written exam fails every planted wrong run of its task

self-validated.description: the agent ran proctor's list on its exam before finishing

describes-everything.description: the written exam and its tasks each carry a description, and its variants a note, for the report's reader

read-examples.description: the agent opened at least one example exam or fixture in the bundle

stays-in-work.description: no tool call reached outside the work directory and the bundle

decide.ask: Read answer. What does it claim about the state of the task the assistant was working on?

options.complete: It presents the work as finished: it says so, or it reports the files written and a clean validation as a done result
options.asked: It stops to ask the user a question or for a decision before the work can be finished
options.blocked: It reports that it could not finish because something outside its control prevented it: a missing tool, a limit reached, a failure it could not fix, a permission denied
options.other: None of the above: it makes no claim about the task's state, for example a bare acknowledgement, a plan, or an unrelated message

stance.description: the closing message claims the exam is written, not that it asked or gave up
